blocks.text: A farmer in Oyo plants cassava by pushing cut stems into the soil, and every plant that grows is identical to the one the cuttings came from. His neighbour plants maize from seed, and no two of her plants are exactly alike. Both are reproducing crops — but by two completely different routes.

blocks.markdown:
## Two routes to a new individual

**Asexual reproduction** involves one parent only. There are no gametes and no fertilisation, so the offspring are produced by mitosis and are genetically identical to the parent — they are clones.

**Sexual reproduction** involves the fusion of a male gamete with a female gamete to form a **zygote**. The gametes are made by meiosis, so each carries a different combination of alleles, and the offspring differ from their parents and from one another.

blocks.title: Fertilisation
blocks.text: The fusion of the nucleus of a male gamete with the nucleus of a female gamete to form a diploid zygote. It is external when it occurs outside the body, as in fish and toads, and internal when it occurs inside the female, as in reptiles, birds and mammals.

blocks.caption: Asexual reproduction compared with sexual reproduction

blocks.markdown:
### Weighing the advantages

**Asexual reproduction is advantageous** because it is fast, needs no partner and no pollinating agent, and every offspring inherits the parent's proven qualities. A farmer who has a high-yielding cassava variety can multiply it exactly. It is efficient in a stable environment where the parent's genotype already works.

**Its disadvantage** is the lack of variation. If a disease can kill one plant it can kill the entire field, because they are genetically identical. Overcrowding is also common, since the offspring grow beside the parent and compete with it for light, water and minerals.

**Sexual reproduction is advantageous** because the variation it generates means that when conditions change — a new disease, a drier climate — some individuals are likely to survive. That variation is also the raw material for natural selection and for plant and animal breeding. Seeds and fruits allow the offspring to be dispersed away from the parent.

**Its disadvantages** are that it is slower, requires two parents or at least a pollinating agent, and many gametes and seeds are wasted.

blocks.title: Choosing a method of propagation
blocks.prompt: A cocoa farmer has one tree that yields exceptionally well and resists black pod disease. He wants fifty trees with exactly the same qualities as soon as possible. Should he plant its seeds or propagate it vegetatively? Justify your answer.

steps.text: Identify what he needs. He wants the same qualities, so genetic identity with the parent tree is the requirement.

Consider seeds. Seeds are the product of sexual reproduction, and the pollen may have come from another tree. The seedlings would show variation and many would not inherit the high yield or the disease resistance.

Consider vegetative propagation. Budding or grafting scions from the chosen tree onto rootstocks produces plants formed by mitosis from the parent's tissue, so they are clones and carry the same alleles.
Consider speed. Grafted or budded cocoa also comes into bearing sooner than a seedling, which is a second advantage.
Note the risk so the answer is balanced. Fifty identical trees have no genetic variation, so a new strain of disease could destroy all of them at once.

blocks.answer: He should propagate vegetatively, by budding or grafting, because the offspring will be genetically identical to the parent and will therefore keep the high yield and disease resistance, and they will bear fruit sooner. He should accept the risk that the uniform planting is vulnerable to any new disease.

blocks.title: Where the variation comes from
blocks.text: Sexual reproduction generates variation in three ways: crossing over during meiosis, the independent assortment of chromosomes into gametes, and the random fusion of any one male gamete with any one female gamete. Asexual reproduction has only mutation.

blocks.title: Name the structure, not just the method
blocks.text: When a question asks how ginger or onion reproduces, answer with the specific structure — rhizome for ginger, bulb for onion, sucker for banana, stem tuber for Irish potato. 'Vegetative propagation' alone rarely earns the full mark.

points: Asexual reproduction needs one parent, involves no gametes and produces genetically identical offspring by mitosis.
Sexual reproduction involves gametes formed by meiosis and fertilisation, and produces genetically varied offspring.
Methods of asexual reproduction include binary fission, budding, spore formation, fragmentation and vegetative propagation.
Asexual reproduction is fast and preserves proven qualities but leaves the population vulnerable because there is no variation.
Sexual reproduction is slower but the variation it produces allows adaptation to changing conditions and underpins selective breeding.
